tools.name: list_covered_countries
tools.description: The countries we research, each with its ISO code and one sourced line, and the mapped countries with the institution that pays their old age pension. Call it when unsure whether a country is researched.

tools.name: country_pension_facts
tools.description: One country's facts: the official free route, what is hard from abroad, what the money is worth and dated obligations. Use it for a question about one country. Quote each fact with its source and read date, and link officialSite or sources[].url where given, else citation.url.

tools.name: check_work_history
tools.description: Start here when a person lists where they worked: for each country, whether a pension is likely and why, the official free route where one applies and any dated obligation. Years may be exact, rough or unknown. Quote each reason with its source and read date, and link officialSite where given, else

tools.name: resolve_employer
tools.description: Use it when a person names an old employer: the country the name points to, the employers we hold it may mean with a confidence from 0 to 1, and for researched employers what it became and its pension plan. Each fact has its source and read date.

tools.name: authority_answer
tools.description: What a national pension institution told us in writing, as published on our answers page, with the institution, the reply date and the link. Use it when a person asks what the authority itself says, and quote the answer as returned.

tools.name: deadline_check
tools.description: Use it when a person left a country or a relative died: the date a departure deadline runs out, from our deadline register, with the official source and read date. Where the start depends on circumstances, the date is an estimate that says what to confirm.

tools.name: create_order_link
tools.description: Only when the person asks to order or what a report costs: our order page with the report and countries filled in, and the fee (Country $99, Enhanced $129 for two countries, Global $149 for three or more countries). The page leads to payment, which opens only if the person pays there. Send no person

tools.name: gpfr_info
tools.description: What GPFR, the Global Pension Finding Register, is, in the caller's language, with the register page, the consent text and its version and, with a country, our fund pages. Show the consent text to the person before gpfr_register. Read only.

tools.name: gpfr_register
tools.description: Registers a person in GPFR after they said yes to the consent sentence from gpfr_info, shown word for word. It sends one confirmation email and the registration stays pending until they click its link. At most 3 emails a day per address.

labels.name: gpfr_fund_count
labels.description: For fund-side agents: how many confirmed people are registered for a pension fund, shown from 10 upwards, otherwise fewer than 10. An aggregate only.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "gpfr_status" appears informational but accepts parameters (code) that enable code/file/secret access.

title: Tool description changed since last scan
detail: Tool "list_covered_countries" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "The countries Pensionarch, each with its ISO code and one sourced line, and the mapped countries with the institution that pays their old age pension." → after: "The countries we research, each with its ISO code and one sourced line, and the mapped countries with the institution that pays their old age pension."

remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
